design.jobs: C3: C at plus3, 10 targets x seeds 12760101, 12760102 = 20 (headline); C1: C at plus1, 10 x seed 12760101 = 10; T3: T at plus3, 10 x 2 = 20; 50 jobs. Smoke seed 12760301 (SJ, KR; C1 and T3) not gated

design.time: SIGKILL at 900 s per job -> KILL; wall_guard_case_s=900 on Certifier34H (was inherited 600 in 075); main cap 4800 s; main run once

diagnostic_not_gated: per-target kill reasons and step counts at C3 vs study 074 sealed; wall_guard events if any; compare IDU walls to 900 vs prior observational 600

gates.GLIVE76: main complete within main_cap+60s; RESULTS matches SEAL; all 50 jobs present
gates.GMEM76: every record has rlimit_as_bytes and workers as designed; kill reasons recorded
gates.GNORESET76: adapter AST ok; every non-KILL record has decoder_objects=1 and resets=0
gates.GS76_sound: 0 WRONG / 0 TRACE_MISMATCH on all recounted records
gates.GSTEP76: over C3 cells where C and T3 both decided, median C/T decoder steps <= 1.0
gates.GTEST76: official TEST_SUITE_076 passed; gated test file hashes match

honest_framing: v0.71.0 (study 075) intended to test JOB_KILL 420->900 s but (1) host reboot lost all sealed records and (2) inherited GUARD_CASE_S=600 fired first, so the 900 s question was never tested (deviation #215). This version keeps certify/34h and JOB_KILL 900 / MAIN_CAP 4800, and applies a MEASUREMENT FIX only: pass wall_guard_case_s=900 into Certifier34H, record it on every C record, and gate that match (GGUARD76). Also persist per-job JSON under results/study-076/main/jobs/ (not /tmp) so a host reboot can still seal recovered records. Not an algorithmic bump; not another pure wall-clock raise beyond 075's intent.
pre_plan_exploration: No gated Brute arm on 076 seeds before lock. Reading of study 075 run.log (observational) and certify16d GUARD_CASE_S=600 source line; no new engine pilot on gate seeds.
process: LEAN: plan locked before data; one main run; exact recount; strict stress; publish failures; ~45-60 min target; no CI; scheduled Actions stay disabled
question: With the same certify/34h API, JOB_KILL 900 s, and the inherited certify16d case guard explicitly set to wall_guard_case_s=JOB_KILL_S (900) so the advertised kill is the effective engine wall, how many real decoders does Brute decide reset-free at a LOOSE declared N (true+3), soundly, and does tight-N hold?
recount: scripts/recount_076.py labels against truth_076; WRONG/TRACE_MISMATCH count as wrong
status_rule: CERTIFIED only if every gate passes; else not certified with failing gate list
target_software: CPython 3.13.5 incremental decoders via public interface only, no resets
what_this_cannot_show: No noise; sizes 3-10 states; N=true+3 uses oracle sizes; two seeds; 2.0 GiB and 900 s are runner caps; guarantee conditional on N and clean readings; fixing the guard tests the intended 900 s wall, not a new algorithm
